source_locator: R2225: ch. V, Actions on the Matanikau; R2226: ch. VI, Action on the Matanikau, 24-26 September
current_activity: attacking across the Matanikau mouth and later covering the withdrawal
notes: Edson, who had taken command of the 5th Marines on 21 September, commanded the combined force on 27 September. Miller, ch. V, and Zimmerman, ch. VI, agree that 2nd Battalion, 5th Marines, failed to establish itself on the west bank at the river mouth, and that after Puller’s battalion was withdrawn the 5th Marines and the raiders also withdrew. Confidence 0.7.

source_locator: R2225: ch. V, Actions on the Matanikau; R2226: ch. VI, Actions on 7-9 October
current_activity: closing on the Japanese bridgehead on the east bank of the Matanikau
notes: Zimmerman, ch. VI, dates the advance from the perimeter to 7 October, when 3rd Battalion, 5th Marines, met a Japanese company east of the river mouth that fell back into a prepared bridgehead. Miller, ch. V, treats the same east-bank fight as the opening of the 7–9 October operation. Confidence 0.7: both histories place the 5th Marines on the east bank that day.

source_locator: R2225: ch. V, Actions on the Matanikau; R2226: ch. VI, Actions on 7-9 October
current_activity: reducing the Japanese bridgehead on the east bank of the Matanikau
notes: Miller, ch. V: on 8 October the 5th Marines and the raiders continued to reduce the east-bank bridgehead, and that night some Japanese tried to break out. Zimmerman, ch. VI, places strong breakout attempts on the night of 7–8 October against the 5th Marines as well, and raider relief on 8 October. The dated row is the 8 October reduction and the night fighting around it. Confidence 0.7.

source_locator: R2225: ch. V, Actions on the Matanikau; R2226: ch. VI, Actions on 7-9 October
current_activity: covering the withdrawal of the force that had crossed the Matanikau
notes: Miller, ch. V: after the 9 October raid the enveloping force recrossed east over the mouth of the Matanikau, and the withdrawal was covered by the 5th Marines. Zimmerman, ch. VI, also places the 5th Marines along the east bank during the operation. Confidence 0.7.

location_qualifier: west bank, short of Point Cruz
source_locator: R2225: ch. VIII, Kokumbona Offensive, 1-4 November
current_activity: crossing the Matanikau and advancing, then halting short of Point Cruz
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: at daybreak on 1 November, after the 11th Marines and 3rd Defense Battalion 5-inch bombardment, the three battalions of the 5th Marines crossed the new footbridges and by 0700 had completed the move. The 1st and 2nd Battalions then attacked, gaining slightly more than 1,000 yards, and halted for the night short of Point Cruz. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. VIII, Kokumbona Offensive, 1-4 November
current_activity: reducing the Japanese pocket at Point Cruz
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: on 2 November 2nd Battalion, 5th Marines, reached the beach west of Point Cruz and trapped the Japanese still opposing the 1st and 3rd Battalions. On 3 November the 5th Marines reduced the pocket, killing about 350 Japanese and capturing guns and machine guns, then was ordered back to the Lunga area. Dated 3 November, the day the pocket was reduced. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. IX; R2227: Part VI, ch. 9
notes: The 5th Marines sailed out of Sealark Channel for Australia on 9 December 1942, the first echelon of the 1st Marine Division to leave (Miller, ch. IX; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9). Confidence 0.7.
